title: Search escalates for FBI fugitive who competed at Salt Lake City's 2002 Olympics - NewsBreak
text:
By Amelia Hobson ,
2 hours ago
Charges are allegations only. All arrested persons are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
SALT LAKE CITY ( ABC4 ) — The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)’s search for a former-Canadian Olympian turned alleged narcotics trafficker has escalated, with an unsealed federal indictment and an increased reward offer.
In 2002, Ryan James Wedding represented Canada in snowboarding at the 2002 Winter Olympics, held here in Salt Lake City. Now, two decades later, Wedding is at the top of the FBI’s ‘Ten Most Wanted’ fugitive list.
“Ryan Wedding’s athletic drive snowballed into a life of violence and, instead of conquering mountains, he mastered a deadly drug distribution enterprise and will continue to order murders while he enjoys protection by his cartel associates and others,” said Akil Davis, the Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office.
FBI officials have reported that Wedding allegedly operates a transnational drug trafficking network that is responsible for over $1 billion in illegal drug proceeds. The FBI also says that Wedding has orchestrated the deaths of several people.
“He controls one of the most prolific and violent drug-trafficking organizations in this world. He is the largest distributor of cocaine in Canada,” said U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi.
In March, the FBI announced that Wedding was on the “Ten Most Wanted” list and offered a $10 million reward for information leading to his arrest. This week, they increased the reward to $15 million.
PREVIOUSLY: Former 2002 Salt Lake City Olympian put on FBI’s ’10 Most Wanted’ list, $10M reward offered They also unsealed a federal grand jury indictment that charged Wedding with overseeing the operations of a criminal enterprise, including by directing others to kill a witness in 2024 and placing a bounty on the victim’s head.
Wedding also allegedly directed the murder of two others, because of a stolen drug shipment.
18 additional defendants were also charged in the indictment for participating in the criminal organization and murders, and seven of the defendants were arrested in Canada today. Among them are Wedding’s attorney, who allegedly advised Wedding to kill the witness.
Courtesy: U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation.
After the indictment was unsealed, the FBI announced an increased collaborative effort to capture Wedding, who is believed to reside in Mexico.
Besides increasing the reward for information leading to Wedding’s arrest and prosecution, the FBI is offering rewards of up to $2 million each for information on wedding’s associates who were involved in the murder of the witness.
The U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control has also reportedly frozen Wedding’s U.S. accounts, limiting his financial capabilities.
“Today’s announcement is a culmination of the steadfast work of the FBI and our partners around the world to identify and dismantle violent gang and drug organizations,” said FBI Director Kash Patel, adding, “This is a clear signal that the FBI will use our resources and expertise to find Ryan Wedding and bring him and his associates to justice.”
“No one, not even a former Olympian, is above the law,” added Senior Bureau Official Chris Landberg of the Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs. “
